chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about cutting the lote tree, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'A man from your companions asked me about it, so I wrote to him: Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) had cut a lote tree and planted grapes in its place.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on cutting Sidr trees and planting other crops in their place?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the practical application of *al-birr* (goodness) in agriculture, where Imam Al-Hasan (AS) personally demonstrated the permissibility of replacing Sidr trees with grapevines to optimize land use. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on beneficial cultivation (*istihlak al-ard*) and the flexibility of fiqh in agricultural matters, provided the change serves a productive purpose.
